links.targetTitle: The Integration Boost strategy is to export the Sky Savings

title: Skybase runs a second demand-side instrument, boosting protocol integrations alongside paying frontend distributors
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2 introduces Skybase's Instances of the Integration Boost Primitive, with Global Activation Status `Active` (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.1.1) and three live Instances in its Active Instances Directory: Euler, Curve and Morpho (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.1.2.1–.2.3). A fourth, Compound, sits in the In Progress Invocations Directory with Invocation Status `Planning` (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.1.4.1).

The counterparty list is categorically different from the Distribution Reward roster. Those were frontends and aggregators — DeFi Saver, CoW Swap, ParaSwap, MetaMask — venues where a user clicks. These are lending markets and an AMM: infrastructure where a stablecoin is *used as collateral or liquidity*, largely without any end user choosing Sky by name.

Both primitives sit under the same parent, Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives (A.6.1.1.4.2.5), so Skybase treats them as two instruments serving one objective: USDS demand. But they buy different things. Distribution rewards buy *acquisition* — new users routed in through an interface. Integration boosts buy *utility* — reasons to hold USDS once you have it, because it works in the venues where capital is already deployed.

The strategic implication is that Skybase's mandate is broader than its own description suggests. A.6.1.1.4.1 frames the Agent around accessible, user-friendly interfaces, yet an entire active primitive is aimed at protocol-level integrations that have no interface dimension at all.
description: The Integration Boost Primitive is Active with Euler, Curve and Morpho Instances and Compound in Planning — targeting lending markets and DEXes rather than user-facing interfaces.
